name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection and analysis of coordinated link-sharing and inauthentic networks on social platforms, the methodological core of Giglietto's research (CooRnet, the vera.ai WP4 alert system, and studies of deceptive information operations). This remains the most active and continuously updated strand of his work, including the 2026 VERA-AI Alert monitoring system.

name: Platform Data Governance & Research Access
description: Work on social media platforms' data policies, API access under the Digital Services Act, and the consequences of platform decisions (CrowdTangle shutdown, Meta's political content reduction, the 100-share threshold) for research and for public visibility of political actors. Reflects his ongoing role as an independent expert for the European Commission's Article 40 DSA data-access process.

name: Generative AI and Disinformation
description: Emerging research on how generative AI is used to produce and scale deceptive content (e.g., AI-generated visuals in coordinated gambling promotion) and on AI-assisted countermeasures, paired with his new 'IA Generativa e Media' course. A clearly growing focus of his current teaching and publication agenda.

name: LLMs for Computational Content Analysis
description: Methodological work integrating large language models into content classification and annotation pipelines for political discourse and complex social phenomena, including validation challenges and comparisons with human coders. Connects to his PhD-level data analysis teaching and recent AoIR collaborations.

name: Political Polarization & Partisanship
description: Studies of partisan attention, hyperpartisan networks, affective engagement in partisan communities, and the broader dynamics of polarization across Italian, German, Brazilian and Latin American contexts, including conceptual work revisiting polarization and populism as analytic categories.

name: Health Misinformation & Fact-Checking
description: Research mapping coordinated networks circulating problematic health content (India, Nigeria) and tools to accelerate COVID-19 fact-checking, extending into trust and 'post-truth' dynamics around medical counter-publics. Reflects a sustained MINE sub-project line funded by the Gates Foundation and Italian MUR.

name: Elections & Social Media Communication
description: Longitudinal program mapping political news coverage and social media dynamics around national elections (Italy 2018/2022, Germany 2021, Brazil), anchored in the MINE research program that Giglietto founded and continues to coordinate as an institutional umbrella.

name: Information Disorder & Fake News
description: Conceptual and empirical work on how false and misleading information circulates within the hybrid media system, including foundational taxonomies of 'fake news' and hateful disinformation — a throughline connecting his theoretical and applied research across two decades.

name: Computational Social Media Research Methods
description: Methodological contributions on using social media and digital trace data for social science research, including survey recruitment via ad platforms, systematic reviews of platform-specific metrics (e.g., Facebook reactions), and the ethics of computational social science — underpinning his Master's and PhD teaching in digital network analysis and data methods.

name: Media Theory & Sociocybernetics
description: Giglietto's theoretical grounding in sociocybernetics and systems theory applied to networked media and social TV/second-screen phenomena — an earlier but still occasionally revisited intellectual foundation (e.g., ISA Sociocybernetics committee involvement) underlying his later empirical work.

name: Platforms, Audiences, and Online Communities
description: Empirical and reflective studies of how platform affordances, cultures, and audience practices shape online sociality, identity, and community formation across sites like Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, Twitter/Mastodon, and LiveJournal.

name: Critical Analysis of AI Industry Imaginaries and Discourse
description: Studies examining how AI industry actors, media, and communities construct and circulate narratives, imaginaries, and framings (e.g., longtermism, techno-hagiography, 'quiet futuring', political-economy 'decoys') that shape public understanding and obscure or legitimize the underlying power structures of AI development.

name: Reflections on the State of Misinformation and Online Harm Research
description: Papers that step back from primary empirical study to critically assess the misinformation/online-harms research field itself — diagnosing biases (e.g., WEIRD-centrism, overreliance on cognitive proxies), mapping gaps in evidence (causal, longitudinal, cross-national), and proposing directions or borrowed lessons (e.g., from climate psychology) to make the field more rigorous and generalizable.

name: Theorizing AI's Social Role: Agency, Trust, and Public Perception
description: Papers that apply or extend social theory and communication-trust frameworks to understand the societal position of AI systems, ranging from conceptual demarcations of machine agency and formal multi-agent social frameworks to models of public trust in generative AI and empirical survey data on public attitudes toward AI adoption.

name: Computational Studies of Political Media and Advertising
description: Papers using large-scale computational or quasi-experimental methods to study political advertising, media capture, and ideological signaling on digital platforms, including causal analysis of ad effects, detection of covert advertiser influence on news coverage, and latent ideology estimation of political video content.

name: Survey Measurement Validity and Comparability
description: Papers examining methodological challenges in survey-based measurement, including whether respondents understand survey questions as intended, how online sample composition and quality checks affect representativeness and response validity, and how question wording and dataset differences affect cross-national and longitudinal comparability of trust measures.
